title: correct-burst-accounting-and-fallback-safeguards-for-dedicated-pool
creator: Maya Chen
description: Critical production escalation: multiple enterprise tenants observed sudden reserved-pool starvation when a single tenant executed a large batched inference job. Symptoms: reserved pool headroom rapidly dropped to 0, burst grants overshot limits, cross-tenant throttling triggered and customer-facing requests returned 503/timeout. This ticket tracked the investigation, hotfix, and rollout of a durable fix + follow-ups.
root_cause: Race in burst token accounting between pool-manager and allocator under high RPC latency. When heartbeat latency exceeded the allocator's window, lease renewals were treated as new grants due to a non-idempotent grant flow and a counter reset path. This allowed a single tenant to double-count available burst tokens and temporarily consume headroom reserved for others.
resolution_summary: Rolled out a two-phased fix: (1) emergency patch v1.21.3 that enforces per-tenant soft cap and immediate throttling to stop runaway consumption; (2) permanent fix in runtime-1.22 introducing monotonic lease IDs, idempotent grant handshake, and a short-lived leader-elected reconciliation to repair inconsistent counters. Verified with canary traffic and inter-region failover tests before global rollout.
steps_taken: 03/10 09:12 - Pager triggered by customer support after AcmeHealth reported 12% request error rate on Dedicated pool EU-WEST2
03/10 09:25 - Triage call with SRE, allocator, and platform oncall; reproduced locally using synthetic high-latency heartbeat script
03/10 11:00 - Applied emergency soft-cap patch (v1.21.3) to EU-WEST2 reserved pools to prevent further cross-tenant headroom starvation
03/11 13:40 - Implemented permanent fix branch: monotonic lease IDs + idempotent grant acknowledgements (PR referenced below)
03/12 02:10 - Canary rollout to 5% of pools with synthetic traffic and customer traffic mirrored; no regressions observed
03/12 14:00 - Gradual ramp to 100% global rollout and monitoring for 48h stabilization
03/13 08:30 - Post-rollout verification and customer communications sent; incident declared resolved
postmortem_notes: Primary contributing factor: optimistic lease renewal logic that assumed low-latency control plane RPCs.
Secondary factor: insufficient integration tests covering allocator heartbeats under high-latency network conditions.
Customer impact window: ~2.5 hours of elevated errors for the affected tenants; mitigation reduced the window to ~30 minutes after emergency soft-cap patch.
Lessons: enforce idempotency on cross-service grant/lease operations, add chaos tests simulating control-plane latency, and harden per-tenant safety nets in allocator.
Communication: targeted emails & Slack threads to affected customers, status page update, and follow-up SRE sync with account teams.
monitoring_changes: Dashboard: Reserved Pool Headroom by tenant + rolling 1h leak detector added to Console release runtime-1.22
runbook_updates: Allocator runbook: new remediation step to immediately apply per-tenant soft-cap and revert to last-known-good grant map
Escalation path: include Allocator lead and SRE pager for any headroom alarm crossing three pools
Playbook: simulating high-latency heartbeat and steps to trigger temporary throttling for safe recovery
tests_added: Integration test: allocator lease renewal under injected 200-500ms RPC latency
Load test: burst grant accounting with 200 concurrent tenants issuing batched jobs
E2E: canary pipeline that mirrors production grant traffic and validates idempotent ack behavior
follow_up_tasks: ENG-423119 - Expand chaos tests to include cross-region control-plane partitions
ENG-423120 - Add metering pipeline check for burst token desync and automated reconciliation job
PM-998 - Customer outreach retrospective and SLA credit proposal for impacted customers
